name: Can you fill a pool without removing the whole shell?

mainEntity.name: Can a swimming pool be filled in without fully removing the concrete shell?
mainEntity.text: Can a swimming pool be filled in without fully removing the concrete shell?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, many pool fill-in jobs do not require full shell removal. A common approach is partial demolition, where the contractor breaks openings in the bottom for drainage, removes the upper part of the shell, and backfills the remaining cavity. This approach can reduce demolition, hauling, and disposal costs. However, leaving part of the shell in place is not ideal for every project. If the yard will support heavy structures later, or if the city requires more complete removal, partial fill-in may not be the best fit. Homeowners should also consider long-term settlement, drainage, and whether the remaining shell could complicate future digging. The right choice depends on budget, site access, and what the property needs after the pool is gone. The contractor should explain exactly how much of the shell stays in the ground and why.
acceptedAnswer.description: Yes, many pool fill-in projects leave part of the shell in place, especially for cost savings. Contractors often punch drainage holes and remove only the upper portion of the structure before backfilling. This is common for partial removals, but it may not suit future construction or all city requirements.
